results.text: Binding site druggability assessment in fragment-based drug design. Target druggability refers to the propensity that a particular target is amenable to bind high-affinity drug-like molecules. A robust yet accurate computational assessment of target druggability would greatly benefit the fields of chemical genomics and drug discovery. Positional isomers of Indolyl-benzodiazepines display dissimilar binding and recruitment of BET transcriptional regulators to targeted genomic loci. BET proteins contain two tandem bromodomains (BD1 and BD2) that bind histone acetyl-lysine residues that can be targeted with small molecule inhibitors such as IBET-762, which bears a triazolo benzodiazepine core.
